title: HelperSessionOutputRows
description: One batch of the rows that left a session's screen, streamed from the helper the moment they left it (nocx-2v80t.3.6). The owner's decision gives the helper no copy of departed rows — ghostty's own scrollback is the buffer — so this document is the only place the rows go. The rows ride in the frame contract's row vocabulary (cells as [grapheme, width, hasText] tuples, styles as per-row runs), encoded by the runtime's own row encoder, so what a coordinator stores from the stream and what it paints live are one shape. Every row is carried exactly once, in stream order; a batch names the absolute index its first row holds, counting every row the session has ever seen depart, so the order is checkable rather than trusted.

fromRow.description: The absolute index of this batch's first row: the count of rows the session had seen depart before it, whether or not any consumer was bound when they did. Indices are the session's, never the consumer's, so a consumer that attaches late continues where the session left off and a confirmed-written mark names a position both ends can check.

lostRows.description: The count of FEEDS the emulator struck immediately before this batch's first row, and never a count of rows: the ABI carries no departure counter, and a prune inside a feed mixes with that feed's own departures in one depth reading, so the rows a prune took are unknowable by contract. An ordinary feed carries none; one struck feed reads as one. A spelling that named lost rows would be a manufactured count.

rows.description: The rows that left, oldest first, in the frame contract's row shape. The array is carried whole: a batch with no rows and a loss marker is how a hole at the very end of an interval is stated, so an empty array is an answer and not an absence.
